title: Gut-Derived Sodium Butyrate Attenuates Liver Fibrosis by Inhibiting Aerobic Glycolysis via the HDAC3/c-Myc Signaling Axis.
authors: Sun, Yong; Wu, Huayue; Zhou, Yutong; Yin, Pengsheng; Wu, Long; Li, Haiyang; Zuo, Shi; Yang, Zhe; Cao, Kun
journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
one_liner_zh: 该文研究肠道代谢物丁酸钠通过HDAC3/c-Myc轴抑制肝纤维化，核心是代谢与信号通路，无蛋白质-DNA互作、结合位点预测或AI/物理模拟建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: Liver fibrosis remains a major global health challenge, driving interest in bioactive metabolites from natural sources as potential therapies. Sodium butyrate (NaB), a gut microbiota-derived short-chain fatty acid with notable anti-fibrotic activity, shows promise, although its mechanisms remain unclear. This study aims to explore the molecular mechanisms through which NaB attenuates liver fibrosis. This study integrates bioinformatics and network pharmacology to predict the molecular targets through which NaB exerts its anti-fibrotic effects. Candidate targets were validated through molecular docking, histopathology, CETSA, and SPR. The inferred mechanisms were further validated in vitro (LX-2 cells) and in vivo (CCl(4)-induced mice) using Western blot, IF Co-IP, RT-qPCR, ELISA, and histopathological staining. HDAC3 was identified as a key driver of liver fibrosis. As a natural HDAC3 inhibitor, NaB markedly attenuated CCl(4)-induced hepatic injury and fibrosis, accompanied by reduced expression of HDAC3, c-Myc, glycolytic enzymes (HK2, PFKFB3, and PKM2), and fibrotic markers (alpha-SMA and type I collagen) in fibrotic liver tissues and LX-2 cells. Mechanistically, NaB exerts its anti-fibrotic effects by inhibiting HDAC3 expression and deacetylase activity, promoting c-Myc acetylation and downregulating its expression, thereby suppressing glycolytic metabolic reprogramming in hepatic stellate cells. These findings indicate that NaB attenuates liver fibrosis by inhibiting HDAC3/c-Myc-mediated metabolic reprogramming, revealing a gut-derived anti-fibrotic mechanism and potential therapeutic targets.
abstract_zh: 肝纤维化仍然是全球性的重大健康挑战，这推动了人们对来自天然来源的生物活性代谢物作为潜在疗法的兴趣。丁酸钠（NaB）是一种源自肠道微生物群的短链脂肪酸，具有显著的抗纤维化活性，显示出应用前景，但其机制尚不明确。本研究旨在探讨NaB减轻肝纤维化的分子机制。本研究整合了生物信息学和网络药理学，以预测NaB发挥其抗纤维化作用的分子靶点。候选靶点通过分子对接、组织病理学、CETSA和SPR进行了验证。推断的机制进一步在体外（LX-2细胞）和体内（CCl(4)诱导的小鼠）中通过Western blot、IF Co-IP、RT-qPCR、ELISA和组织病理学染色进行了验证。HDAC3被确定为肝纤维化的关键驱动因子。作为一种天然HDAC3抑制剂，NaB显著减轻了CCl(4)诱导的肝损伤和纤维化，并伴随纤维化肝组织和LX-2细胞中HDAC3、c-Myc、糖酵解酶（HK2、PFKFB3和PKM2）以及纤维化标志物（alpha-SMA和I型胶原）表达的降低。在机制上，NaB通过抑制HDAC3表达和去乙酰化酶活性，促进c-Myc乙酰化并下调其表达，从而抑制肝星状细胞中的糖酵解代谢重编程，发挥其抗纤维化作用。这些发现表明，NaB通过抑制HDAC3/c-Myc介导的代谢重编程来减轻肝纤维化，揭示了一种肠道来源的抗纤维化机制和潜在的治疗靶点。
